review.assessment:
This change restricts recursive flattening by gating the recursion behind a `depth > 0` condition, preventing unconditional deep unwrapping. It also replaces array reassignment via `.concat()` with in-place mutation using `.push(...)` and spread syntax, which is functionally equivalent but cleaner given `result` is never reassigned.

No defects were identified. The implementation correctly handles the default depth of 1, arbitrary positive integers, zero/negative depths (by halting recursion immediately), and `Infinity` (which remains `Infinity` after subtraction in JS, allowing complete flattening without parameter drift). All host measurements passed without issues.
